title: Priority-aware residency routing with dynamic allow/deny precedence and emergency escape handoff
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a tenant-aware routing policy that enforces EU-only data residency while allowing safe, auditable operator exceptions and an automated emergency escape handoff path. This ticket scopes the core runtime and control-plane changes required to: (1) evaluate per-request residency constraints, (2) resolve allowlist/denylist precedence at tenant and account levels, (3) select a tiered fallback model variant when EU capacity is saturated, and (4) provide an emergency escape handoff that preserves audit trails and limits cross-border egress to mitigated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime evaluates residency metadata and enforces EU-only routing for tenants with residency=EU
Allowlist and denylist can be configured at tenant and account levels; precedence semantics documented and implemented (denylist > tenant-level allowlist > account allowlist)
When EU capacity unavailable, system selects an approved fallback variant and applies an egress risk score; fallback only used if tenant has explicit opt-in for fallback or emergency escape enabled
All cross-region fallbacks generate audit events including decision reason, selected model variant, toggles used, and operator id
Admin console shows simulated routing outcome before enabling emergency escape for a customer
Unit + integration tests cover precedence permutations and emergency escape manual/automated flows
Performance regression within +/- 5% p50 latency for routing decision path under 99th percentile request volume
Security review completed and sign-off recorded in ticket
steps: Add tenant residency flag to control plane schema and propagate to routing PDP (policy decision point)
Define policy DSL entries for allowlist/denylist precedence and emergency escape gating
Implement routing decision path in gateway: evaluate tenant->account->global lists, residency tag, capacity signals, and fallback policy
Extend model catalog metadata with 'fallback_variant' and 'egress_risk' attributes
Introduce 'simulate' API to preview routing decisions for a given tenant and request metadata
Wire audit events to observability pipeline (cloud-logs) with structured fields for regulatory reporting
Add admin console controls for enabling emergency escape per-customer with justification notes
testing_plan: Automated matrix tests that iterate tenant residency (EU/non-EU), allow/deny combinations, capacity state (healthy/saturated), and emergency toggle (on/off)
Integration test that deploys a small canary region and validates fallback selection to pre-approved variant using synthetic traffic
E2E policy simulation test in staging with sample tenants and recorded audit logs reviewed by compliance
Performance test: measure routing decision latency under 10k rps simulated load
Chaos test: simulate EU region outage and validate graceful fallback and operator alerting
rollback_plan: If new routing causes incorrect routing, disable new PDP in control plane feature flag and revert gateway to prior routing module
Revoke emergency escape toggles rolled out in last 24 hours and re-run simulation for affected tenants
If audit pipeline errors occur, route audit events to durable queue (S3) while fix deployed
Follow postmortem and re-enable changes only after root cause and compensating controls validated

notes: Trade-offs considered: implementing full per-tenant allowlist/denylist evaluation in gateway increases routing latency by ~1-2ms but centralizes enforcement; alternative was to push policy to control plane with a cache, which reduces per-request cost but complicates consistency under rapid changes.
Egress cost: cross-region fallback will incur egress charges and potential contractual/regulatory blockers. Fallbacks must be whitelisted per-tenant and flagged in billing exports.

Operational runbook: when emergency escape is enabled for a tenant, SRE will receive a high-priority pager and a dedicated short-lived audit log will be created documenting the operator, justification, and TTL.
Migration: will migrate 5 pilot tenants with legal approval before general availability. Use simulate API and 'dry-run' admin toggle for pilots.
Metrics to monitor: fraction of requests routed outside residency, fallback-selection-rate, audit-log-delivery-failure-rate, routing-decision-latency-p99
